Eight behaviors confirmed against Microsoft's live rendering-troubleshooting page before authoring: (1) limited CSS margin/padding, fix is padding on td elements (quoted verbatim); (2) no CSS background images on sections — VML with pre-calculated height; (3) a TRANSPARENT background-color is treated as a background image, fix is fully-opaque color; (4) VML rounded buttons on VML backgrounds lose their border radius; (5) forwarding inserts gaps, workaround is the [if gte mso 9] zero-height row with mso-line-height-rule:exactly (markup taken from the page); (6) word-break is all-or-none and   makes a phrase one unbreakable word; (7) line height renders larger than web clients; (8) malformed HTML renders as a solid black body. Also 600–800px width guidance and rounded-VML-buttons-break-on-forward.

Dark-mode rules confirmed against Microsoft's email dark-mode guidance: clients invert/replace background COLORS but generally preserve background IMAGES; avoid pure #000000/#FFFFFF (they trigger inversion) in favor of #1A1A1A/#F5F5F5; transparent-background logos with stroke/glow; no text embedded in images; square buttons for compatibility; sender cannot opt out of client transforms.

Three outcomes, not two — supported, DROPPED (parser rejects it, logged 'unknown property'), and INERT (parses, logs nothing, does nothing). Corrections to the first draft: `transform` and `border-radius` are SUPPORTED and the draft wrongly discouraged transform; `aspect-ratio` is DROPPED, which is the concrete reason figures must be sized in mm; `animation`/`transition`/`will-change`/`scroll-behavior` are inert with NO warning, so they were split out as lint W007 because one rule covering both groups described the second wrongly. probe_css_support.py re-measures all 33 rows and reports DRIFT on upgrade.

id.symbol: the linter discriminates rather than merely runs

rationale: Negative control (probes/flawed.html, every defect deliberate): 7 errors, 8 warnings, exit 2. Positive controls (clean.html, selfcontained/doc.html): clean, exit 0. Three real defects were found by running it and fixed at source, not documented away. (1) The @page check was satisfiable by a COMMENT mentioning @page — the negative fixture's own header comment silenced E003 — so comment bodies are now blanked before every check, with newlines preserved so line numbers stay true. (2) It followed <link rel=stylesheet> but not @import, so E003 (an ERROR) fired on a correct factsheet whose @page lived in the imported base sheet. (3) It read `font-family: var(--family-display)` as a family name and reported W004. Both false positives surfaced only when the linter met a real template, never on the fixtures.

id.symbol: strict-fetch contains but does not gate; FatalURLFetchingError is not an Exception

rationale: Probed with a control (the out-of-tree stylesheet loads fine WITHOUT the flag, so the test is not vacuous). With --strict-fetch the fetch is refused and named precisely, but WeasyPrint turns the refusal into a log line and FINISHES — so the default outcome of the security flag is a PDF quietly missing an asset, which for a factsheet means shipping without a logo. Hence --fail-on-fetch-error, wired to URLFetcher's own fail_on_errors. Building that gate then exposed a defect of the same family the repo keeps hitting: FatalURLFetchingError subclasses BaseException, NOT Exception, so the worker's `except Exception` could not catch the one error the gate exists to raise — it died with a traceback and empty stdout and render.py reported 'unknown error'. Found by running the gate, not by reading it. Also settled: base_url is BOTH the relative-path root and the strict-fetch root, so widening it to reach a sibling assets/ dir breaks the template's own paths — a strict-fetch bundle must be self-contained under one directory.
grounded_by: probe:render.py --strict-fetch/--fail-on-fetch-error with positive and negative controls

id.symbol: the factsheet fails closed and renders two pages

rationale: Full pipeline run on a fictional volatility-carry index: validate -> Jinja2 StrictUndefined -> lint clean -> render 2 pages, with the running footer (audience label + identifier + 'Page N of 2') on both pages and the mandatory blocks present. The gate's discrimination was proved on six injected defects, each caught with a specific message at exit 2: missing as-of date, future as-of date, free-text period, a pre-formatted return string, disclaimer prose smuggled into disclaimer_blocks, and a hand-authored disclaimer_text. The empty fonts/ slot behaved as designed — exactly four 'Font-face cannot be loaded' warnings, loud rather than silent. One QA iteration was needed and found a real defect: the first render was 3 pages because page 1 overflowed by the risk table, stranding it alone; fixed by pairing returns and risk side by side. NOT verified: no page IMAGE was ever looked at (poppler is a system binary, unavailable), so the layout is plausible, not seen — recorded as the standing gap in both PROBES.md files.

id.symbol: closing keywords: list, default-branch condition, one-per-issue syntax

rationale: GitHub docs list exactly close/closes/closed, fix/fixes/fixed, resolve/resolves/resolved. They work in a PR description or a commit message, but ONLY when the PR targets the default branch; against any other branch they are ignored and no link is created. In a commit message the issue still closes on merge into the default branch, but the PR is not listed as linked. Cross-repo form is KEYWORD owner/repo#N, and several issues need the full keyword each ('Resolves #10, resolves #123'). The docs do not say whether a keyword in a PR COMMENT works, so no asset claims it does. The templates' 'Done when' line and the /epic and /issue commands rest on this row.

id.symbol: sub-issues: 100 per parent, 8 levels, sub_issue_id is the id not the number, parent endpoint

rationale: The docs state 'up to 100 sub-issues per parent issue and up to eight levels of nested sub-issues'. The REST page lists GET /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}/parent and GET/POST .../sub_issues. POST's body takes sub_issue_id (integer), described as 'the id of the sub-issue', which must share the parent's repository owner. It is the database id, NOT the #number, and the MCP tool's schema repeats the warning ('ID is not the same as issue number'). The MCP issue_write create also accepts parent_issue_number, which creates and links in one call, so the commands prefer it and the trap never arises. The docs do NOT say that a parent closes when all its sub-issues close. That gap is why the epic-autoclose workflow exists, and no asset claims either behaviour for GitHub itself.

id.symbol: cascade happens in-run because GITHUB_TOKEN events start no new workflow runs

rationale: GitHub docs: 'events triggered by the GITHUB_TOKEN will not create a new workflow run', except workflow_dispatch, repository_dispatch, and some pull_request types. When the workflow closes a parent, that closure fires NO second run for the grandparent, so a design that relied on re-triggering would silently stop one level up. The script therefore walks up the chain itself, bounded by the documented 8-level nesting limit.

id.symbol: epic auto-close/reopen script behaves as specified

rationale: probe_epic_autoclose.py extracts the workflow's own run: script, so it cannot drift from what ships. It runs the script under real bash, curl, and jq against a local fake of the sub-issue endpoints, asserting the exit code and the exact write list. Result: 14/14, including four no-write controls (open sibling, open parent on reopen, no parent, parent closed by hand) and two fault cases (HTTP 500 on the parent lookup or the sub-issue list exits non-zero with ::error:: and closes nothing). The probe was itself checked against five deliberate breaks, each turning at least one case red: errors read as 'no parent', no cascade, open siblings ignored, reason always 'completed', and a case-sensitive repo compare. NOT verified: a live GitHub run. The fake serves the documented shapes. The first real epic to close is the confirming event.

id.symbol: issues-triggered workflows run only from the default branch

rationale: GitHub's events reference, issues section: 'This event will only trigger a workflow run if the workflow file exists on the default branch.' An installed epic-autoclose.yml does nothing until it merges into the default branch. That explains why a copy on a feature branch looks installed but never fires. Recorded in mechanics.md and /epic step 7. The installed copy (.github/workflows/) is kept byte-identical to the canonical asset by a drift check in the probe, which was shown to fail on an appended line.

id.symbol: PR template locations and default-branch availability

rationale: GitHub docs: a single PR template may live at the repo root, in docs/, or in .github/ as pull_request_template.md. Multiple templates go under a PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/ directory and are chosen with the `template` query parameter. 'Templates are available to collaborators when they are merged into the repository's default branch', so the installed .github/pull_request_template.md does nothing until its PR merges. The docs do not say whether the filename is case-sensitive, so the skill lists the spellings it detects and makes no claim either way.

Run through the hook's own stdin interface with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set. It is silent on the clean factory tree and on example-project, which has no .github/ (an uninstalled copy is not a defect: the negative control). It reported each injected defect by name: a line appended to the installed PR template, a line appended to the installed epic-autoclose.yml (both caught in one run), a manifest source that does not exist, and a manifest that is not JSON. It returns to silent after restoring. This replaces the drift check that lived in probe_epic_autoclose.py, which ran only when someone ran the probe. The hook runs on every git commit/push via git_guards.py.
grounded_by: probe:asset_integrity.py via stdin, 6 runs (2 clean controls, 4 injected defects)

id.symbol: markdown issue templates: required frontmatter, name length, default-branch availability

rationale: GitHub docs: a markdown issue template in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ must contain 'valid name: and about: keys in the YAML frontmatter'. The template name 'must be more than 3 characters'. title, labels, type and assignees are optional frontmatter keys. Templates become available 'once these changes are merged into the default branch'. The docs do NOT say what happens when a template names a label the repo lacks, so the installed templates set no labels (the commands choose labels from the repo's existing set), and only the epic sets a title prefix. issue_body.py lint-templates enforces name > 3 characters and a present about:, and probe_issue_body.py proves the lint can fail. YAML issue forms were rejected on purpose: API-filed issues bypass forms, and a form cannot share a source with the render path.
